title: Present Continuous
tagline: now and around now: am / is / are + -ing
why: We use the present continuous for what is happening right now or for a short time around now. It helps you describe what you see, explain why you're busy, and talk about changes.
know: the -ing spelling rules: make → making, sit → sitting, lie → lying
common state verbs that don't usually take -ing: know, want, need, believe, own
understand: the difference between a habit (I work) and something happening now (I'm working)
why we say I know, not I'm knowing
able: say what you and other people are doing at the moment
describe temporary situations: I'm working nights this month.
talk about changes: More people are working from home.
mistakes: She is wear a red coat.
I am knowing her very well.
use: actions happening now: Shh! The kids are sleeping.
temporary situations around now: I'm working nights this month.
changing trends: The city is getting busier.
signals: now, right now, at the moment, today, this week, this month, these days, currently, still, Look!, Listen!
tip: Ask: is it happening now, or is it a habit? I drive to work (every day), but I'm taking the train this week (my car is at the garage). State verbs like know, want, believe stay simple, even now.

pick.q: Please be quiet. I ___ on the phone.
pick.why: It is happening now: am + -ing. 'I talking' has no am.

pick.q: Look out the window! It ___ again.
pick.why: Look! tells us it is happening now: It is raining.
Understand is a state verb, so we don't use -ing: I understand what you mean.

pick.q: We ___ our kitchen this month, so we're eating out a lot.
pick.why: A temporary situation around now: are painting. 'We painting' has no are.
Present continuous questions start with am, is or are. With you, use Are.

pick.q: He ___ a new phone. His old one is broken.
pick.why: Need is a state verb, so we don't use -ing: He needs a new phone.

pick.q: Our neighbourhood ___ more expensive these days.
pick.why: A change happening around now: is becoming. These days is a clue.
Questions: question word + are + you + -ing. Why are you looking at me?

type.q: Turn the music down. The baby ___ (try) to sleep.
type.why: Happening now: is + -ing. Try keeps the y: trying.

type.q: The kids ___ (swim) in the lake right now.
type.why: One vowel + one consonant at the end: double it. swim becomes swimming.

type.q: I ___ (not / work) this week. I'm on vacation.
type.why: A temporary situation: I am not working this week.
A question about now: What are you cooking?

type.q: She ___ (sit) in the waiting room at the moment.
type.why: At the moment = now. Sit doubles the t: sitting.

type.q: My son ___ (study) for his driving test these days.
type.why: A temporary activity around now. Keep the y before -ing: studying.

type.q: We ___ (stay) at my sister's place this week.
type.why: This week = a temporary situation: We are staying.

type.q: He ___ (make) dinner, so he can't come to the phone.
type.why: Happening now. Drop the final e: make becomes making.

spot.q: I am wanting a glass of water.
spot.why: Want is a state verb, so we don't use -ing: I want a glass of water.

spot.q: Listen! Someone knock at the door.
spot.why: Listen! means it is happening now: Someone is knocking at the door.

spot.q: They are siting near the window.
spot.why: Sit ends in one vowel + one consonant, so double the t: sitting.
In questions, are comes before the subject: Where are you going?
The negative needs is: She isn't working today.

order.a: What are you reading at the moment?
order.why: Question word + are + you + -ing: What are you reading?

order.a: My brother isn't working this week.
alt: This week my brother isn't working.
order.why: Isn't + -ing for a temporary situation: My brother isn't working this week.

order.a: More people are cycling to work these days.
alt: These days more people are cycling to work.
order.why: A trend around now: are cycling. These days can go at the start or the end.

order.a: Are you still looking for a new job?
order.why: Are + you + still + -ing. Still goes before the -ing verb.

pick.q: Turn off the stove! The water ___.
pick.why: It is happening now, so use is + -ing: The water is boiling.
Believe is a state verb, so we don't use -ing: I believe you.

pick.q: They ___ in the garden right now.
pick.why: Right now = present continuous: They are working.

pick.q: ___ she still talking on the phone?
pick.why: She takes is: Is she still talking on the phone?
A change around now: is getting. 'The weather getting' has no is.
Belong is a state verb, so we don't use -ing: This bag belongs to me.

type.why: Look! = now. Drop the final e: shine becomes shining.

type.q: I ___ (wait) for you outside the station.

type.why: Question: why + is + the baby + -ing. Why is the baby crying?

type.q: We ___ (not / watch) this show. You can turn it off.
type.why: Not happening now: We aren't watching this show.

type.q: He ___ (run) in the park right now.
type.why: Run ends in one vowel + one consonant, so double the n: running.

type.q: These days my English ___ (improve) because I practise every day.
type.why: These days = a change happening around now. Drop the final e: improving.
Question about now: Who are you talking to?

type.q: The dog ___ (lie) on the sofa again!
type.why: Verbs ending in -ie change to -ying: lie becomes lying.

spot.why: Look! means it is happening now: The bus is coming.

spot.q: I am not believing his story.
spot.why: Believe is a state verb, so use the present simple: I don't believe his story.

spot.q: She is writeing an email to her manager.
spot.why: Drop the final e before -ing: write becomes writing.

spot.q: Is he work from home today?
spot.why: After is, use the -ing form: Is he working from home today?

order.a: Why are you wearing your winter boots?
order.why: Why + are + you + -ing: Why are you wearing your winter boots?

order.a: The children are playing video games upstairs.
order.why: Are + -ing for an action now: The children are playing video games.

order.a: She is taking an online course this month.
alt: This month she is taking an online course.
order.why: A temporary situation: is taking. This month can go at the start or end.

bank.q: Can you answer the door? I ___ a shower.
bank.why: It is happening now. Have can take -ing when it is an action: I am having a shower.

bank.q: I ___ two brothers and a sister.
bank.why: Have meaning own or family is a state verb, so no -ing: I have two brothers.
Everyone is singular, so use is: Everyone is waiting for us.
Right now = present continuous. Question order: What is she doing?

bank.q: These days, my daughter ___ to learn Korean.
bank.why: These days = a temporary activity around now: is trying.

bank.q: He ___ the answer to this question.
bank.why: Know is a state verb, so we don't use -ing: He knows the answer.

bank.q: I can't come out. I ___ for an exam.
bank.why: Something happening around now: I am studying for an exam.

bank.q: Look at those clouds! The sky ___ dark.
bank.why: Look! = a change happening now: The sky is getting dark.

bank.q: Sorry about the mess. We ___ (plan) a trip to Quebec City at the moment.
bank.why: At the moment = now. Plan ends in one vowel + one consonant, so double the n: planning.
These days = a temporary situation: I am not sleeping well.

bank.q: Where ___ (they / go)? The office is the other way.
bank.why: A question about now: Where are they going?

bank.q: My colleague ___ (use) my computer, so I can't check my email.
bank.why: Happening now. Drop the final e: use becomes using.

bank.q: Please be quiet. We ___ (record) a video.
bank.why: Happening now: We are recording a video.

bank.q: I am needing some help with this form.
bank.why: Need is a state verb, so no -ing: I need some help with this form.

bank.q: They is playing cards in the kitchen.
bank.why: They takes are: They are playing cards in the kitchen.

bank.q: My sister is working in Halifax this year.
bank.why: Correct! This year = a temporary situation, so is working is right.

bank.q: He is liveing with his parents for now.
bank.why: Drop the final e before -ing: live becomes living.

bank.a: What is your daughter studying at university?
bank.why: What + is + your daughter + -ing: What is your daughter studying?

bank.a: I am not using the car today.
alt: Today I am not using the car.
bank.why: Am + not + -ing: I am not using the car today.

bank.a: Is it still snowing in Toronto?
bank.why: Is + it + still + -ing. Still goes before the -ing verb.
